title: Temperature
about: Turn one setting to make a chatbot more predictable or more surprising.

cards.prompt: Chatbots have a **temperature** setting: slide it until **mat** has at least **80%**.
cards.hint: Slide both ways and watch the bar for "mat". Which way makes it grow?
cards.nudge: Watch "mat": if its bar shrinks, go the other way; if it grows, keep going.
cards.explanation: A **low** temperature makes the likeliest word even likelier. Turn it right down and it's "mat" almost every time.

cards.title: Turning the dial
cards.body:
**Temperature** changes how the model uses its chances.

- **Low:** the likeliest word gets even likelier. Predictable.
- **1:** the chances stay as learned.
- **High:** the chances even out. Surprising, sometimes nonsense.

The top word always stays on top. When one word has nearly all the chance, even a fairly high temperature usually picks it.

cards.prompt: More surprising now: slide until **no word** is above **45%**.
cards.hint: The top word is the one to bring down. Which way evens the chances out?
cards.nudge: "mat" must drop below 45%, so go the way that shrinks its bar, and go far.
cards.explanation: Only a **high** temperature brings "mat" below 45%. Press "Generate 5": the cat sometimes sits on the moon. More surprising, and more nonsense.

cards.prompt: "mat" has 60% at temperature 1. You turn it right **down** and run it **10** times. What happens?

options.text: It picks "mat" about 6 times out of 10
options.nudge: That's temperature 1. What does a very low one do to the top word?

options.text: It picks a different word each time
options.nudge: That's closer to what a very high temperature does.
Low temperature helps the top word, it doesn't hide it.

cards.hint: What does a very low temperature do to the top word's chance?
cards.explanation: A very low temperature makes the top word's chance shoot up, so it's "mat" **almost every time**. About 6 in 10 is what temperature 1 gives.

cards.prompt: Same temperature: two story ideas come out different, but "2 + 2" gives 4 both times. Why?

options.text: It's sure of "4", but story ideas have similar chances
It remembers its first idea and avoids repeating it
options.nudge: Each time, it just works out chances and picks. How sure is it each time?

options.text: Stories are harder, so it keeps getting them wrong
options.nudge: A story idea can't really be wrong. How many good next words does each have?

options.text: Sums use a stricter temperature than stories do
options.nudge: The temperature is the same, so the difference must be in the chances.

cards.hint: Picture the chances for each: one clear winner, or lots of close ones?
cards.explanation: When one word has nearly all the chance, like "4", it's picked every time. When many have similar chances, like story ideas, the picks vary.

cards.prompt: **One right answer**? Use a low temperature. Want **variety**? Go higher. Sort each job.
cards.hint: Is there one right answer, or do you want lots of different ideas?
cards.nudge: Which jobs have one right answer, so want the likeliest word every time?
cards.explanation: Maths, summaries and spelling have **one right answer**: low. Band names, poems and story twists want **variety**: higher. Most apps set the temperature for you.

cards.prompt: A model's top pick for Australia's capital is **Sydney** (it's Canberra). You turn the temperature right down. What happens?

options.text: It switches to "Canberra": low is careful
options.nudge: Temperature never changes the order of the words. Which is on top?

options.text: It says "Canberra" more: low favours truth
options.nudge: Low temperature favours the top word, whatever it is. Is it true here?

options.text: It says each city about equally
options.nudge: Evening out is what a high temperature does. What does a low one do?

cards.hint: Low temperature makes the **top** word win. Which is on top, and is it true?
cards.explanation: A low temperature makes the top word win, and here it's wrong. Temperature changes **how** it picks, never **what it knows**.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- **Temperature** changes how a model picks; the order never changes.
- Low: predictable, for one right answer. High: variety, then nonsense.
- It changes how it picks, never what it knows.

Next: why chatbots sometimes make things up.
